Welcome & Purpose Slide 2 of 50

Welcome & Purpose

Speaker: Prof. Andrew H. Volk

  • Welcome families, friends, faculty, and students.
  • Opening prayer led by Prof. Andrew H. Volk, Chapter Advisor and Permanent Correspondent.
  • Recognize the significance of the chapter’s first induction ceremony.
  • Frame the evening as both celebration and commissioning into a community of mathematical scholarship.
Pi Mu Epsilon exists for the promotion and recognition of scholarly activity in the mathematical sciences.
Transition to Emma Kay for “About Pi Mu Epsilon.”
About Pi Mu Epsilon Slide 3 of 50

About Pi Mu Epsilon

Speaker: Emma Kay

  • Founded at Syracuse University and incorporated in 1914.
  • A national honor society devoted to promoting mathematics and recognizing student achievement.
  • Chapters encourage scholarship through talks, writing, conferences, mentoring, and mathematical community.
PME encourages undergraduate presentations and posters, supports chapter activity, and sponsors a journal accessible to undergraduate students.
Transition to Avery Morrison for “Virginia Omicron at Liberty University.”
Virginia Omicron Slide 4 of 50

Virginia Omicron at Liberty University

Speaker: Avery Morrison

  • Tonight marks the first induction ceremony of the Virginia Omicron Chapter.
  • This chapter represents an enduring commitment to scholarship, service, and mathematical growth at Liberty University.
  • It also connects Liberty students and faculty to a national community of chapters across the United States.
Suggested spoken emphasis
A chapter is both an honor and a stewardship.

Pi Mu Epsilon Scholarship Pledge

Speaker: Heidi Jackson

All candidates please stand and repeat in unison:

“I solemnly promise that I will exert my best efforts to promote true scholarship, particularly in mathematics; and that I will support the objectives of the Pi Mu Epsilon Honor Society.”
After the pledge: “Thank you. Please be seated.”

Book Signing & Math Prompts Slide 47 of 50

Membership Book Signing & Mathematical Prompts

Speakers: Dr. Daniel Scott Joseph and Prof. Andrew H. Volk

  • As each student signs the membership book, they respond to one of five prompts.
  • Prompt choices: (1) Share a favorite math memory, (2) Describe a time math brought extreme joy or pain, (3) Name your favorite math topic, (4) Identify one math skill you wish you had learned earlier, or (5) State the highest level of math you hope to study.
Transition to Prof. Andrew H. Volk for symbols and motto.
Symbols & Motto Slide 48 of 50

Symbols & Motto

Speaker: Prof. Andrew H. Volk

  • Colors: violet, gold, and lavender.
  • The seal, shield, and logo visually connect members to the wider Society.
  • Motto: To Promote Scholarship and Mathematics.
Transition directly into the charge to new members.
Charge to New Members Slide 49 of 50

Charge to New Members

Speaker: Prof. Andrew H. Volk

  • Pursue mathematical excellence with humility, integrity, and intellectual honesty.
  • Use your gifts in service to others and in encouragement of younger students.
  • Help Virginia Omicron become a chapter known for scholarship, initiative, and community.

Your achievement tonight is both recognition and responsibility. May you continue to love what is true, seek what is difficult, and share what is beautiful in mathematics.
